title: 割集与割集 KCL
statement: 电路如图（V_s1 = 10 V，I_s5 = 1 A，R_1 = 2 Ω，R_2 = R_3 = 4 Ω，R_4 = R_5 = 2 Ω，R_6 = 8 Ω）。画有向图时把 V_s1 与 R_1 的串联看成一条支路（支路 1），把 R_5 与 I_s5 的并联看成一条支路（支路 5），其余每个电阻一条支路；结点编号 1、2、3、4（4 接地），支路编号与方向见下方的有向图。
图中画出了两条闭合线 Q_1、Q_2。判断哪些支路集合是割集，并用割集形式的 KCL 求一个支路电流。

questions.ask: 割集 Q_1（包围结点 1 的闭合线）包含哪些支路？
choiceExplain: 少了支路 1：结点 1 仍经支路 1 连到结点 4。
支路 3 接在 2、3 之间，不与结点 1 相连，闭合线也不穿过它；多了它就不是“最少”的集合。
对：闭合线穿过的支路就是割集支路。包围单个结点的割集就是这个结点上的全部支路，割集 KCL 就是结点 KCL。
少了支路 6（接在 1、3 之间）：只去掉 1、2，结点 1 仍经 6 与其余部分相连。
questions.explain: 割集：去掉这些支路，图恰好分成两部分；少去掉任何一条，图仍连通。

questions.ask: 下面哪一组支路**不是**割集？
choiceExplain: 这是 Q_2：图分成 {2, 3} 和 {1, 4} 两部分，四条支路都跨在两部分之间。
包围结点 4 的割集：结点 4 上的全部支路。
对：去掉这 5 条支路，只剩支路 3，图分成 {1}、{4}、{2, 3} 三部分，不满足“恰好两部分”（不是最少的）。
questions.explain: 判断方法：去掉这组支路后数一数分成几部分（必须恰好两部分），再看每条支路是否都跨在两部分之间。

questions.ask: Q_2 的割集 KCL：已知 I_2 = 1.1 A、I_5 = 0.4 A、I_6 = 0.5 A（都按支路方向），求 I_4。
选定任意一棵树后，基本割集有几个？
questions.explain: 每条树支确定一个基本割集（只含一条树支，其余都是连支），所以基本割集数 = 树支数 = n − 1 = 3。

hints: 割集是“一组支路”：去掉它们图恰好分成两部分，而且少去掉任何一条都不行。
闭合线穿过的支路就是这个割集的支路；包围单个结点时就是结点 KCL。
割集 KCL：流出闭合面的支路电流代数和为零——先按支路方向判断每条支路是穿出还是穿入。
solution: **Q_1。** 包围结点 1，穿过支路 1、2、6：结点 1 的全部支路，割集 KCL 就是结点 1 的 KCL。

en.title: Cut-sets and cut-set KCL
statement: The circuit is drawn below (V_s1 = 10 V, I_s5 = 1 A, R_1 = 2 Ω, R_2 = R_3 = 4 Ω, R_4 = R_5 = 2 Ω, R_6 = 8 Ω). In the graph, V_s1 in series with R_1 counts as one branch (branch 1), R_5 in parallel with I_s5 as one branch (branch 5), and each other resistor as one branch; the nodes are numbered 1, 2, 3, 4 (4 is grounded) and the branch numbers and directions are those of the directed graph under the circuit.
Two closed curves Q_1 and Q_2 are drawn on the graph. Decide which sets of branches are cut-sets, and use KCL for a cut-set to find a branch current.

questions.ask: Which branches belong to cut-set Q_1 (the closed curve around node 1)?
choiceExplain: Branch 1 is missing: node 1 is still connected to node 4 through it.
Branch 3 (between 2 and 3) does not touch node 1 and is not crossed; with it the set is no longer minimal.
Right: the branches the curve crosses form the cut-set. A cut-set around one node is just all branches at that node, and its KCL is the node equation.
Branch 6 (between 1 and 3) is missing: removing only 1 and 2 leaves node 1 connected through 6.
questions.explain: A cut-set: removing its branches splits the graph into exactly two parts; putting back any one of them reconnects it.

questions.ask: Which set of branches is **not** a cut-set?
choiceExplain: This is Q_2: the graph splits into {2, 3} and {1, 4}, and all four branches run between the two parts.
The cut-set around node 4: all branches at node 4.
Right: removing these 5 branches leaves only branch 3; the graph falls into {1}, {4} and {2, 3} — three parts, so the set is not minimal.
questions.explain: Test: remove the set and count the parts (exactly two), then check that every branch of the set runs between the two parts.

questions.ask: KCL for cut-set Q_2: given I_2 = 1.1 A, I_5 = 0.4 A, I_6 = 0.5 A (all along the branch directions), find I_4.
questions.explain: Count currents leaving Q_2 as positive: branches 4 and 5 point out of {2, 3}, branches 2 and 6 point in, so I_4 + I_5 − I_2 − I_6 = 0 → I_4 = 1.1 + 0.5 − 0.4 = 1.2 A.

questions.ask: How many fundamental cut-sets does any tree give?
questions.explain: Each tree branch defines one fundamental cut-set (one tree branch plus links), so there are as many as tree branches: n − 1 = 3.

hints: A cut-set is a set of branches whose removal splits the graph into exactly two parts, and no smaller part of it does.
The branches crossed by a closed curve form its cut-set; around a single node this is the node equation.
Cut-set KCL: the algebraic sum of the branch currents leaving the closed surface is zero — first decide from each branch direction whether it leaves or enters.
solution: **Q_1.** It surrounds node 1 and crosses branches 1, 2, 6: all branches at node 1, so its KCL is node 1's KCL.

**Which sets are cut-sets.** Removing {1, 2, 4, 5, 6} leaves branch 3 only and the graph falls into {1}, {4}, {2, 3} — three parts, **not** a cut-set; {2, 4, 5, 6} (Q_2), {1, 4, 5} (all branches at node 4) and {1, 2, 6} (Q_1) are cut-sets.
**KCL for Q_2.** Q_2 surrounds nodes 2 and 3. From the branch directions, 4 (2→4) and 5 (3→4) leave, 2 (1→2) and 6 (1→3) enter: I_4 + I_5 − I_2 − I_6 = 0 → **I_4 = 1.2 A**.
**Number of fundamental cut-sets** = number of tree branches = **3**.
